triagePrinciples: Research further only when uncertainty can materially change a structural family, city/regional variation, repetition rule, bespoke decision or defining spatial grammar.

Preserve shared-family caveats and intentional exclusions rather than forcing symmetric cross-city families.

questions.title: Elche Ciudad Jardín villa kit boundary
questions.unresolvedQuestion: Is the Ciudad Jardín detached-house condition sufficiently represented by the shared Mediterranean-villa structure, or does its current plot/building grammar require a distinct Elche city-specific variation?
questions.whyItMatters: Phase 2 isolated Ciudad Jardín as a meaningful detached-house family, but its final kit boundary remains explicitly unresolved.
questions.recommendedAction: Sample current built plots and repeated house/site relationships in the affected zone, focusing on setbacks, parcel scale, party-wall incidence, roofs and street-edge treatment.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolve shared-regional versus Elche-specific treatment.
Retain bounded qualitative ranges rather than false dimensional precision.
Do not generalize the result to Palmeral or pedanía housing.
sourceIssueStatements: Exact current Ciudad Jardín villa grammar remains insufficiently calibrated for a final kit boundary.

questions.title: Málaga eastern hillside villa / compound boundaries
questions.unresolvedQuestion: Do Cerrado, Pinares and Candado share one Málaga hillside-villa/compound variation, or do their plot, slope and building relationships justify multiple city-specific subprofiles?
questions.whyItMatters: The three zones represent a major topography-driven city condition that cannot be reduced to a flat-land villa palette.
questions.recommendedAction: Compare representative slope relationships, retaining walls, access, setbacks, compound organization, roof form and repeated development patterns across the three zones.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolve one-versus-multiple Málaga hillside subprofiles.
State what remains shared with the regional detached-villa archetype.
Record slope/site grammar separately from facade styling.
sourceIssueStatements: Current villa/compound patterns remain insufficiently calibrated for final hillside-family boundaries.

questions.title: Murcia Infante and secondary postwar-estate calibration
questions.unresolvedQuestion: How should Infante and adjacent Buenos Aires postwar fabric be classified relative to Murcia’s already separated La Paz, La Fama and Vistabella subtypes and the shared open-block/perimeter families?
questions.whyItMatters: Phase 2 successfully decomposed Murcia’s best-known eastern estates; leaving Infante coarse could reintroduce a generic estate treatment into an important contiguous urban area.
questions.recommendedAction: Sample block/site organization, height bands, access/open space and repeated building forms in the two affected zones, explicitly comparing them with the three already researched east-estate profiles.
acceptanceCriteria: Assign Infante/Buenos Aires to existing subtype(s) or justify one new city-specific subtype.
Avoid creating a new top-level shared family unless cross-city evidence requires it.
Document regeneration/infill separately from original estate grammar.
sourceIssueStatements: Infante and other postwar areas outside the three east estates need stronger typology calibration.

questions.title: Murcia resort-housing family placement
questions.unresolvedQuestion: Which current Sucina–Gea y Truyols resort-housing forms belong back in the shared detached-villa or rowhouse/townhouse families, and which remain a distinct Murcia resort variation?
questions.whyItMatters: The closeout portfolio deliberately excludes Murcia resort housing from the shared low-rise family pending current subtype sampling.
questions.recommendedAction: Sample representative resort compounds and house types, focusing on attachment, plot/communal-space relationship, roof, facade rhythm and repetition by development.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolve shared-family membership at subtype level.
Retain resort site grammar even where building structure is shared.
Do not treat all outer Campo housing as resort morphology.
sourceIssueStatements: Resort/industrial facade and plot sampling remains incomplete before final production-kit boundaries are frozen.

sharedIndexUnresolvedStatements.statement: Murcia resort housing is deliberately excluded pending current subtype/facade sampling; future comparison may place individual resort forms back into shared detached/rowhouse families.

questions.title: Murcia Polígono Industrial Oeste production-kit boundary
questions.unresolvedQuestion: What plot/building subtypes distinguish the logistics core from the service fringe of Polígono Industrial Oeste, and how much can remain within the shared industrial/logistics structural kit?
questions.whyItMatters: The structural industrial family is stable, but the final production-kit boundary between logistics sheds, service frontage and ancillary buildings remains explicitly unresolved.
questions.recommendedAction: Sample representative current plots in both zones, separating building form from yard/loading/parking/site grammar.
acceptanceCriteria: Define a bounded industrial subtype set.
Confirm whether all subtypes remain parameterized variants of the shared industrial/logistics family.
Avoid promoting purely site-layout differences into unnecessary new structural families.
sourceIssueStatements: Resort/industrial facade and plot sampling remains incomplete before final production-kit boundaries are frozen.

questions.title: Elche business-park kit calibration
questions.unresolvedQuestion: Does Elche Parque Empresarial need a stronger Elche-specific variation within the shared Elche–Málaga business/technology-park family?
questions.whyItMatters: The cross-city family is already high-confidence, so further research is only valuable if production needs a more specific facade/roof/site kit boundary.
questions.recommendedAction: Research only if prototyping shows the current shared structure cannot reproduce Elche’s business-park identity. Sample a small set of representative office/logistics buildings rather than expanding general park facts.
acceptanceCriteria: Either confirm the existing shared family plus parameterized city variation or document one bounded Elche-specific subtype.
Do not reopen Alicante membership without new evidence.
sourceIssueStatements: Business-park facade/roof typologies remain insufficiently sampled for final shared-versus-city-specific kit calibration.

questions.title: Alicante northern-estate subtype calibration
questions.unresolvedQuestion: Do Virgen del Remedio, Lo Morant, Juan XXIII and Colonia Requena need further production-facing subdivision within the shared open-block estate family?
questions.whyItMatters: Phase 2 already established the top-level family. Additional research should occur only if a prototype cannot express the meaningful estate-to-estate differences with existing subprofiles.
questions.recommendedAction: Compare representative blocks and site organization only where current subtype definitions prove insufficient in prototyping.
acceptanceCriteria: Preserve the shared open-block family unless evidence requires a bounded Alicante subtype.
Do not make block-by-block cataloging a completeness goal.
sourceIssueStatements: Northern-estate classification is improved but still not complete block by block.

questions.title: Benidorm peripheral low-density / villa grammar
questions.unresolvedQuestion: Do Benidorm’s peripheral low-density zones require a city-specific villa/low-rise subtype, or can they remain regional detached/rowhouse structures with local site parameters?
questions.whyItMatters: These zones are secondary to Benidorm’s tower identity and the issue is medium severity, so research should be conditional on production need.
questions.recommendedAction: Sample representative low-density forms only if these peripheral zones are important to the playable/rendered extent or if current regional kits visibly misrepresent them.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolve city-specific versus regional treatment without overfitting fringe morphology.
Keep boundary/transition uncertainty separate from building-form conclusions.
sourceIssueStatements: Peripheral villa/low-density facade, roof and site grammar remains weakly sampled.

questions.title: Portfolio current-state and transition recheck
questions.unresolvedQuestion: What is the as-built state of all planned, partially built, transition, regeneration, industrial-growth and infrastructure-change zones at the production freeze date?
questions.whyItMatters: These uncertainties are time-sensitive by definition. Researching them now would create stale certainty; they should be verified near production freeze while preserving current/future separation.
questions.recommendedAction: At production freeze, re-check only the listed zones against current authoritative/as-built evidence. Record changes as state updates, not retroactive corrections to the Phase 2 evidence history.
acceptanceCriteria: Every affected zone has an explicit freeze-date state: existing, partially built, transition, planned, brownfield or other supported status.
Future proposals remain separate from current built form.
Conexión Sur and industrial/growth occupancy are checked with date-stamped evidence.

questions.recommendedAction: Preserve the shared family as a structural reuse authority and express differences through subtype/parameter constraints; do not research merely to force a false universal typical range.
